title: Argenta Biotech Q2 2026 Renewal Narrative & Tailored Slide Notes
content:
Purpose:
This document is a working draft of the Q2 2026 executive narrative and per-slide speaking notes for the Argenta Biotech renewal conversation. Objective is to coordinate CS + Solutions to present a concise value story, surface risk early, and outline a clear ask ladder that preserves expansion upside.

Meeting objectives (30–40 minute exec session):
- Reconfirm outcomes: reduce inference latency for large batch genomics pipelines and lower per-token inference cost by 20% compared to current Dedicated baseline.
- Share usage & quality trends: show steady adoption across 3 internal teams (Genomics, Assay Analytics, Data Platform).
- Present renewal options and recommended path (12-month committed Dedicated with pilot Private VPC for regulated workloads).
- Agree next steps and owners for procurement, security review, and pilot kick-off.

Guiding narrative (1-minute opener):
- "Argenta has successfully embedded Redwood across pre-production genotype processing and two upstream feature pipelines. This quarter we focused on throughput stabilization and lowering unit costs; the data shows consistent latency improvements and fewer model regressions. Our proposal preserves Argenta's performance SLAs while offering a path to further cost reductions and private deployment for regulated assays."

Suggested slide order + speaker notes (short bullets per slide):
1) Title + Meeting Agenda (Maya)
  - Quick agenda: outcomes, usage, quality, ask ladder, next steps (30–40m).
  - Frame conversation as alignment, not negotiation.

2) Exec snapshot (Maya -> 2 minutes)
  - 3 metrics: 30-day p95 latency, tokens per sample, monthly committed spend vs actual.
  - Call out headline: "p95 latency down 18% since tuning batch policy in Dec 2025."

3) Adoption map (Ethan)
  - Show teams using API, sample volumes by pipeline, peak concurrency windows.
  - Note: Genomics batch jobs concentrated 01:00–05:00 UTC (opportunity for burst scheduling to reduce cost).

4) Quality & Reliability (Priya)
  - Regression gauge: 3 flagged prompts in Jan, all resolved by model pin and eval rollback.
  - Incident note: one retry loop on 2026-01-22 (root cause: transient NVMe perf), SRE mitigation and auto-fallback to variant model since Feb.

5) Cost & Optimization (Maya)
  - Current effective cost per 1M tokens, comparison to initial Dedicated baseline.
  - Opportunities: enable KV prefix caching for long-context sample templates and adopt int8 quantized variant for batch inference. Estimated incremental savings: 12–18%.

6) Proposed renewal ladder (Maya)
  - Option A (Recommended): 12-month Dedicated commit with 20% discount + 3-month Private VPC pilot (zero up-front) to validate compliance controls.
  - Option B: 6-month renewal at standard Dedicated rates with staged Private conversion.
  - Option C: month-to-month hosted at current rates (highly flexible but higher unit cost).
  - Visual: tradeoff table (cost vs. control vs. time-to-value).

7) Risk heatmap & mitigation (Priya)
  - Risk: Security review delay — mitigation: supply SOC2 bridge report and engage Security Solutions engineer for a biweekly checklist.
  - Risk: Model quality regression on new assay prompts — mitigation: pre-commit eval harness + canary rollout policy.

8) Case study & ROI snapshot (Liam)
  - Short before/after for SamplePrep pipeline: 25% throughput gain, 14% direct token cost reduction after batching and kernel tuning.
  - Include quote from Argenta eng lead (paraphrased) about developer velocity.

9) Ask & decision timeline (Maya)
  - Ask: verbal alignment on Option A within 2 weeks; final contract by end of Q2.
  - Decision owners: Procurement review (A. Novak), Security sign-off (Dr. R. Chen), Platform lead (S. Morales).

10) Next steps & owner table (table on slide)
  - Deliverables: SOW draft (Maya), Pilot onboarding checklist (Ethan), Security artifact bundle (Priya).
  - Dates: pilot kickoff target 2026-04-15, contract signed by 2026-06-30.

Tailored talking points by stakeholder:
- CTO (A. Novak)
  - Focus: strategic architecture, vendor lock-in risk, long-term unit economics.
  - Talk track: present Dedicated + Private pilot as the low-risk path to both control and predictable economics. Call out the plan to allow a rollback to hosted in rare cases.

- Head of Bioinformatics (Dr. R. Chen)
  - Focus: model fidelity, reproducibility, audit trails for regulated assays.
  - Talk track: emphasize canary model rollouts, eval harnesses, and audit logs in Console. Offer a 2-week focused eval on the model set used for clinical variant calling.

- Procurement (Procurement lead)
  - Focus: pricing, SLA, exit conditions.
  - Talk track: explain discount ladder tied to committed spend; show clear exit/fallback clauses for Private deliverable if compliance not met within pilot window.

Renewal negotiation ladder (phrased as asks):
- Tier 0: Agreement-in-principle on Option A (commit + pilot).
- Tier 1: Procurement approves term sheet; Security accepts pilot artifact list.
- Tier 2: Contract signature and 30% of reserved capacity invoiced at start.

Health metrics & backup numbers (brief):
- 30-day active API keys: 7 (3 production, 4 dev/test).
- Avg tokens/sample: 4.8k (peak pipelines up to 18k).
- 30-day p95 latency: 420ms (down from 510ms on 2025-11-01).
- Error rate (5xx): 0.04% (noted spike on 2026-01-22 incident).
- Monthly effective cost per 1M tokens: $67 (estimated after current discounts).

Risk & open questions (notes to internal team):
- Security will ask for KMS key usage demonstrable plan. Action: Priya to map Redwood KMS flow to Argenta's encryption policy.
- Compliance timeline: Argenta needs Private VPC readiness window — confirm whether network peer timelines can match pilot target.
- Pricing escalation: Procurement will push for higher discount for a 24-month commit. Prepare counter with measured cost-savings projection tied to batching/quantization adoption.

Appendix (for share-after-meeting):
- Raw charts: weekly throughput, latency percentiles, error traces.
- Sample prompts that triggered earlier regressions and which evaluation tests were added.
- Proposed pilot checklist: access matrix, acceptance criteria (throughput, latency SLO, audit log delivery), test dataset pointers.

Meeting logistics (prep checklist):
- Pre-read deck circulated 3 business days prior (Maya).
- Invite list: CTO, Head of Bioinformatics, Procurement, Platform lead, SRE liaison (optional).
- Runbook: 10-minute technical deep-dive on pilot architecture scheduled with Platform lead if needed.

Notes to CS presenter (Maya):
- Keep opening under 60s and use numbers (latency %, cost $) — executives react to crisp metrics.
- When price pushback starts, reframe to unit economics and demonstrate quick wins (enable caching, small quantization) that reduce spend within 4–6 weeks.
- If Security stalls, offer a tightly scoped pilot with an explicit compliance gating checklist rather than a full Private deployment up-front.

Draft status log:
- 2026-02-15: initial draft (Maya).
- 2026-02-20: added incident postmortem notes (Priya).
- 2026-02-28: cost sensitivity analysis added (Ethan).
- 2026-03-04: review version for CS leadership.

Open tasks (owners & ETA):
- SOW draft for Option A (Maya) — due 2026-03-11.
- Security artifact pack (Priya) — due 2026-03-09.
- Pilot onboarding plan & infra checklist (Ethan) — due 2026-03-15.

End of draft.

Comments: This QBR narrative is intentionally concise; slides should be visually sparse with 3 key metrics per slide. Keep the appendix dense so technical teams can deep-dive post-meeting.
